📉 More accounts. Fewer crypto trades

eToro’s latest results reveal an unusual split between user growth and trading activity.
The platform ended the second quarter with 4.28 million funded accounts, an increase of 18% year over year.

But its July crypto figures moved in the opposite direction:
• crypto trades fell 73% year over year to 1.4 million
• the average amount invested per crypto trade declined 50% to $182

At the same time, eToro reported that its overall number of trades remained flat, with equities helping drive the company’s growth.

The conclusion is not that users are abandoning financial platforms.
It is that account growth and crypto activity are two different signals.

A larger user base does not automatically create more trades. Participation depends on market conditions, volatility, confidence and whether investors see enough opportunity to act.

Registrations measure access.
Trading activity measures conviction.
In the current market, the distance between the two remains significant.
